title: Relative latching maps give lifts of arbitrary ordinal diagrams
statement:
Let $\mathcal B$ be a category admitting all small colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and let $\theta$ be any small ordinal, regarded as the category with one arrow $\beta\to\alpha$ precisely when $\beta\leq\alpha$. Let $D,E,U,V:\theta\to\mathcal B$ be functors and $f:D\to E$, $p:U\to V$ natural transformations. For $Z:\theta\to\mathcal B$ put $L_\alpha Z=\operatorname{colim}_{\beta<\alpha} Z_\beta$, with its canonical map to $Z_\alpha$. The induced maps define the relative latching map
$$\lambda_\alpha(f):D_\alpha\amalg_{L_\alpha D}L_\alpha E\longrightarrow E_\alpha,$$
where the pushout is the colimit of the displayed span. Suppose that, for every $\alpha<\theta$, $\lambda_\alpha(f)$ has the left lifting property against $p_\alpha$, with the diagonal property of [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. Then $f$ has the left lifting property against $p$ in the functor category: for every pair of natural transformations $s:D\to U$ and $t:E\to V$ satisfying $ps=tf$, there exists a natural transformation $h:E\to U$ with $hf=s$ and $ph=t$. No continuity condition is imposed on any of the four diagrams. The assertion includes the empty ordinal and requires no model structure or factorization system. All indexing categories are small in fixed universes, which may be enlarged.
